# API Requirements Quality Checklist: MOEX Ticker History API

**Purpose**: Review the clarity and completeness of the API and MOEX data requirements
**Created**: 2026-10-07
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are the response fields, requiredness, types, and null rules stated consistently for all six fields? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003–FR-005]
- [x] CHK002 Does the spec define whether `facevalue` represents the value currently reported for the ticker or the value effective on each historical date? [Gap, Spec §FR-005]
- [x] CHK003 Does the spec define how the service determines a ticker's primary board when board listings or primary-board designations change over time? [Gap, Spec §FR-011]
- [x] CHK004 Are MOEX historical-data access requirements and any required subscription or credentials documented as an external dependency? [Dependency, Gap, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK005 Does the spec make clear that all upstream pages must be included to satisfy the requirement to return all available daily records? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK006 Is the allowed `SYMBOL` format defined precisely enough to distinguish malformed symbols from valid but unknown tickers? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK007 Are the client-error and upstream-dependency HTTP status codes and error response shape explicitly defined in the feature requirements? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008–FR-009]
- [x] CHK008 Is the meaning and unit of `volume` explicit, including its distinction from monetary turnover? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK009 Do the nullable-field rules in FR-003 and FR-005 align with the requirement that every record contains all six fields? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003–FR-005]
- [x] CHK010 Do the success criteria distinguish daily-history fields from reference-data fields such as `facevalue`? [Consistency, Spec §SC-002, FR-005]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK011 Are the sample tickers and source dates for comparing returned values with MOEX ISS identified objectively? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001–SC-003] — Named comparison case: `SBER`, trading date `2026-10-06`.

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK012 Are requirements complete for an unknown ticker, a valid ticker with no history, and a ticker that cannot be resolved to a primary board? [Coverage, Spec §US-1, FR-007–FR-009, FR-011]
- [x] CHK013 Do failure requirements distinguish invalid client input, upstream unavailability, denied history access, and unusable source records? [Coverage, Exception Flow, Spec §US-2, FR-009]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK014 Are requirements defined for nullable numeric market fields while preserving a valid trading date for ordering? [Coverage, Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases, FR-003–FR-004]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK015 Are any required response-time, throughput, or availability targets explicitly stated, or is their omission an intentional scope decision? [Gap, Spec §Success Criteria]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK016 Are the primary-board selection rule, full-history boundary, and face-value time scope recorded as confirmed requirements or clearly marked assumptions? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions, FR-006, FR-011]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK017 Is “primary board associated with that ticker” unambiguous when the requested history spans a ticker's multiple board listings? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-011]
- [x] CHK018 Does the meaning of “facevalue” in the example align with the source and time semantics defined for each historical record? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-003–FR-005]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- This checklist evaluates requirement quality, not implementation behavior.
